outcome: Give students reliable, multilingual answers and guided service completion across approved institutional information.
overview: Students lose time searching fragmented websites and portals for routine answers, while service teams repeat the same guidance every term. This assistant answers in Arabic and English from approved institutional content only, cites the source and date behind every answer, and completes low-risk service steps once the student has authenticated. Sensitive, welfare or uncertain matters are refused and handed to the named human team with the full conversation context. An eight-to-ten-week controlled pilot runs on an agreed set of approved intents, targeting measurable containment, complete citation coverage and faster first response, with safeguarding drills, permission tests, accessibility checks and an auditable record of every conversation.

benefits.text: Resolve a target 30% of the approved routine intents without human handling, at the agreed answer-quality threshold
benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue; to validate against the institution’s own contact baseline
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate in a controlled pilot on a fixed intent set — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Give students consistent Arabic and English answers around the clock, each carrying a citation and the date of the source content
benefits.source: Reference design — retrieval is restricted to approved content and citation is enforced structurally
benefits.limits: Answer accuracy depends on content owners keeping the approved knowledge base current; stale sources produce stale answers

benefits.text: Release student-services staff time from repeated routine enquiries towards complex casework and peak-period cover
benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue — avoided handling and improved capacity
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on intent coverage and on whether released hours are actually redeployed

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (UAE, KSA); student records, conversation logs and transcripts stay inside the institution’s tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No maintained knowledge base and no named owner for answer content
notFor.why: The assistant only answers from approved sources; without owned, dated content it has nothing safe to retrieve and citations cannot be trusted

notFor.situation: The institution wants the assistant to give counselling, immigration or legal advice
notFor.why: The design refuses and escalates on welfare, safeguarding and regulated-advice intents by policy — it does not act as a counsellor or adviser

notFor.situation: No identity provider and no service APIs for timetable, fee or application status
notFor.why: Permission-aware answers and low-risk service completion both depend on authenticating the student and calling a system of record

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the institution owns approved content, the intent scope, safeguarding policy and privacy approval · Duration: 6–10 weeks pilot; 12–20 weeks to production deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, conversational-AI engineer, integration engineer, accessibility tester; customer knowledge content owner, IT service owner, safeguarding lead, data-protection officer · Support model: Business-hours support with peak-period escalation cover at enrolment and results; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery, contact baseline and intent prioritisation
2) Knowledge remediation and content ownership
3) Assistant, retrieval and integration build
4) Safety, safeguarding and red-team testing
5) Accessibility, load and permission testing
6) Controlled pilot and benefit review

Safe escalation demonstrated on welfare and out-of-scope intents
Accessibility and load tests passed, with analytics and audit proven end to end
Content owners complete UAT and accept the review cadence
